metadata.title: Non-cognitive skills and social gaps in digital skills: Evidence from ICILS 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICILS 2018 microdata for 8th-grade students and constructs the dependent variable as the CIL plausible values (five PVs) for the Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) test. The analytic sample is restricted to cases with non-missing values on key variables; the authors explicitly state they listwise-deleted missing values, yielding 40,403 students. Because ICILS is a complex multistage survey, the authors obtain point estimates by applying ICILS survey design weights and compute standard errors using replicate weights included in the ICILS dataset, implemented via the R package survey. They also note that country/region/city-level weights are not available, so they use a fixed-effects approach with mean-centering at the school level to focus on within-student variation while still using student-level survey weights.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used ICILS 2018 8th-grade student data for the CIL test plausible values and background questionnaire variables. The analysis excludes students with missing values on key variables via listwise deletion, resulting in an analytic sample of 40,403 students. The study does not use teacher/headmaster data. To address the nested structure (students within schools within countries/regions/cities) while avoiding unavailable country/region/city weights, all variables are mean-centered at the school level and the models are estimated as fixed-effects linear models using only student-level data with survey weights.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2018 Grade 8 Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) test (plausible values)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Fixed-effects linear models with survey weights and replicate-weight SEs (R²/Adj. R² by model): Model 1 R²=0.09 (Adj. R²=-0.04); Model 2 R²=0.31 (Adj. R²=0.20); Model 3 R²=0.18 (Adj. R²=0.05); Model 4 R²=0.14 (Adj. R²=0.00); Model 5 R²=0.37 (Adj. R²=0.24). Coefficients in Model 5: Female=5.39***; Parental higher education=8.83***; Migrant=-9.31***; Time drop=0.67***; Performance drop=117.65***; Item response rate=119.17***.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2018 Grade 8 CIL plausible values the study leveraged Gender, Parental higher education, Immigrant background, and non-self-reported non-cognitive proxies (Drop in response time and Drop in performance) to predict CIL test score, finding that adding the non-cognitive proxies substantially improves model fit (Adj. R² increases from -0.04 in the baseline to 0.24 in the full model) and narrows the gender and socioeconomic gaps while leaving the immigrant gap reduced but still negative. This indicates that accounting for students’ test-taking effort and persistence-related behaviors can materially change measured digital-skills inequalities, so accountability and cross-country comparisons should adjust for such non-cognitive factors rather than relying on raw score gaps alone.

data.outcome_summary: The paper analyzes ICILS 2018 8th-grade Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) plausible values (five PVs combined using Rubin’s rules) for 12 participating countries/regions/cities, with a final analytic sample of 40,403 students after listwise deletion of missing key variables. The authors estimate fixed-effects linear models with school-level mean-centering to address the nested design and apply ICILS survey design weights for point estimates, with replicate weights for standard errors, using the R survey package. The baseline model (only student characteristics) has low explanatory power (Adj. R² = -0.04), while adding non-self-reported non-cognitive proxies improves fit markedly (Adj. R² = 0.20–0.24; best in Model 5 with R² = 0.37). The strongest proxy is drop in response time, and including proxies reduces the gender and socioeconomic gaps; the immigrant gap also shrinks but remains statistically significant. Limitations include the absence of causal identification and the use of behavioral proxies that may partially reflect cognitive capacities.
